name: Enabot EBO Air 2
description: A small, self-righting rolling home-monitoring robot with a 2K camera (current EBO Air 2 generation; the original Air, still pictured here, shipped with 1080p), two-way audio, and AI person/pet detection. Roams and patrols manually or autonomously rather than mapping the home with LiDAR/SLAM.

specs.label: Battery
specs.note: 4–7 hr runtime, 2–3 hr charge; original Air was 2500mAh/~2–6 hr

specs.label: Weight
specs.note: original Air figure; Air 2 not independently confirmed

specs.note: 137° FOV, IR night vision; original Air was 1080p/~118° FOV

specs.note: no LiDAR/SLAM mapping on this model line

specs.note: wire-free, 20–55 cm/s, climbs up to 4° slopes (Air 2 spec)

specs.note: 32GB included, up to 256GB — no mandatory cloud

sourcing: Verified against Enabot's own official site (enabot.com, store.enabot.com) and independent reviews from Android Central, iMore, Digital Camera World, and TechAdvisor, which cover the original Ebo Air's established track record. This entry's display name and lead specs (price, camera resolution, mobility) were updated to the current EBO Air 2, confirmed via Enabot's own EBO Air 2 product page, Home Depot, and Best Buy listings ($149 regular $199, 2K/2304×1296, 137° FOV). Enabot also sells a further "Air 2 Plus" step-up and, historically, an "Air 2S" variant. Chewy's own listing for the original (non-"2") Air reads "Discontinued," while it is still listed for sale on Enabot's own site and Amazon as of this check — an inconsistency worth flagging rather than resolving one way. No LiDAR/SLAM navigation should not be confused with the pricier Ebo X, which does map the home.

pricing.summary: Enabot's own store lists the current **EBO Air 2** at **$149** (regularly $199), in Dove White, Jay Blue, or Robin Pink. The original Ebo Air covered in earlier versions of this entry was officially listed around $199–$229, with sale prices as low as $119 — that older model's availability is now mixed (see the note below), so treat the Air 2 pricing above as the current reference figure.

editorial.heading: Sensors & Hardware
editorial.body: The EBO Air 2 is a self-righting, ball-shaped robot on a silent brushless-motor wheel base with anti-drop sensors, moving wire-free at 20–55 cm/s and climbing slopes up to 4°. Its camera shoots 2K (2304×1296, 137° FOV) with IR night vision — an upgrade from the original Air's 1080p/~118° FOV sensor. It has no LiDAR or SLAM mapping — reviewers flagged this as the original's weakest area, causing bumps and getting stuck, and nothing suggests Air 2 changed that. Storage defaults to local microSD rather than mandatory cloud.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: The original Ebo Air has been succeeded by the EBO Air 2 — this entry now tracks the Air 2 as Enabot's current model, adding Air 2 Plus (AI chat mode via GPT/Gemini) as a further step up. Air 2 stores video locally on a microSD card (32GB included, expandable to 256GB) rather than requiring a cloud subscription — a specific, sourced differentiator from many competing home-monitoring cameras — carrying forward the original's several-years-long track record confirmed across multiple independent reviewers (Android Central, iMore, Digital Camera World, TechAdvisor). Availability signals for the original Air specifically are mixed — Chewy lists it as discontinued, while it remains listed on Enabot's own store and Amazon — so a buyer encountering "Ebo Air" listings should confirm which generation they're actually looking at.

firmwareCommunity.note: Enabot has not released a public SDK, firmware repo, or developer API for Ebo Air. Not currently listed in Builds & Mods.
